rules.wave: A wave is a maximal run of records on one (pid, conn) whose [t, t+ms] intervals overlap; a describe record is always its own wave and the record after it starts a new one. Statements are execute and simple records; describes and connects count only as round trips.
rules.transaction: Records between begin and commit/rollback on one (pid, conn). publication = has the lock_timeout 1s set_config and the counter lock (INSERT INTO persistence_counters(key)); group publication = also has >= 1 member attribution (SELECT set_config('gbrain.write_request',...)); admission = INSERT INTO persistence_requests; claim = UPDATE persistence_requests [r] SET state='running' (head claim and group follower claim are separate occurrences); cursor = INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE op_checkpoints.
rules.freeze: Per admission: sync-process statements outside any phase transaction from the end of the first cursor save after max(previous admission end, last publication commit) up to the admission begin; waits and consumer background excluded. Wall excludes the cursor saves nested in the window.
rules.prepare: Per publication: statements outside any phase transaction between the end of the last claim since the previous publication and the publication begin (waits and consumer background excluded).
rules.wait: Per admission: WRITE_PROGRESS_SQL and SELECT * FROM persistence_requests WHERE id=$1::uuid / id=ANY($1::uuid[]) reads from the admission commit to the next cursor save (or admission). Its wall overlaps claim, prepare and publication.
rules.commit_gap: Between consecutive committed group publications of one sync process (all publications when it published no group): wall, and every record the process sent in between. Single publications include foreground writes the sync process's consumer published.

rules.member_chain: Members are split at their attribution statements (with its describe, if any): segment i runs from member i's attribution to member i+1's, so it holds member i's apply/effects tail and member i+1's authorize/snapshot/validate lead. The rotation leaves the steady per-member total unchanged. Steady = segments 2..n-1 of transactions with >= 3 members; segment 1 carries first-use describes, the last one runs into the counter lock and is part of the fixed cost.
rules.counter_hold: From the counter row lock (SELECT * FROM persistence_counters ... FOR UPDATE, with its describe) to the commit, inclusive. INSERT INTO persistence_counters(key) ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING creates missing rows and locks no existing one, so it is outside the hold.
